question: A train covers 216 km in 3 hours. What is its average speed in meters per second?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Speed = Distance ÷ Time = 216 ÷ 3 = 72 km/h

To convert from km/h to m/s, multiply directly by 5/18.

Speed in m/s = 72 × (5/18) = 20 m/s

**∴ The correct answer is 20 m/s.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 Distance = 216 km
 Time = 3 hours
 Speed = ? m/s
 

**Given:**

⇒ Distance covered by the train = 216 km

⇒ Time taken = 3 hours

**Formula Used:**

⇒ Speed = Distance ÷ Time

⇒ Speed in m/s = Speed in km/h × (5/18)

**Calculation:**

⇒ Speed = 216 ÷ 3

⇒ Speed = 72 km/h

⇒ Convert km/h into m/s by multiplying with 5/18

⇒ Speed = 72 × (5/18) m/s

⇒ Speed = 4 × 5 = 20 m/s

**∴ The correct answer is 20 m/s.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Unit Conversion

To convert km/h to m/s, multiply the value by 5/18. To convert m/s to km/h, multiply by 18/5.

Average Speed

Average speed is defined as the ratio of total distance traveled to total time taken. Formula: Average Speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time.

Relative Speed

If two bodies move in the same direction at speeds S₁ and S₂, their relative speed is |S₁ − S₂|. In opposite directions, it is S₁ + S₂.

Train Crossing an Object

When a train of length L crosses a stationary object of length x (like a platform or bridge), the total distance covered is L + x.
